beats.label: rumble
lines: Ever wonder why your belly sometimes sounds like a drum?
Your gut is a tube that constantly pushes contents forward.
Gas and liquid moving create vibrations we hear as rumbling.

beats.label: MMC cycle
lines: Between meals, a cleaning wave called the migrating motor complex sweeps the stomach every two hours.
This wave is the main source of the hungry growl.

beats.label: echo
lines: An empty stomach lets the sound echo, and the hunger hormone ghrelin spikes.
When you hear a growl, check how long since your last meal—about two hours means the MMC is active.
You’ll hear the rhythm of your own digestive housekeeper!

sources.claim: Stomach rumble is produced by movement of gas and fluid in the intestines as they are propelled by peristalsis.
The migrating motor complex occurs every 90–230 minutes (about two hours) during fasting and causes the rumbling when hungry.
When the stomach is empty, ghrelin is produced and contributes to the sensation of hunger and louder sounds.
Around two hours after the stomach has been emptied, it sends signals to the brain and the MMC restarts, producing growls.

youtube.title: Why does your stomach growl? 🤔
youtube.description: Learn the science behind those noisy belly growls and how the migrating motor complex works.
